list: The official 55 PS5 trophies: 1 platinum, 2 gold, 6 silver, 46 bronze. 28 hidden on PSN.
releaseNote: GTA VI released 19 Nov 2026. Names, descriptions and grades are as PlayStation publishes them (mirrored by Exophase and PSNProfiles). Every guide below is written in our own words from the sources in data/sources.json; where guides still disagree or a hidden trophy's method is unconfirmed, this guide says so instead of inventing an answer.
title: Vice City Neon — GTA VI Trophy Guide & Platinum Tracker

trophies.guide: The platinum pops on its own the moment the other 54 trophies are yours. There is no separate task, no extra mission and no way to earn it early. Use the tracker: when it reads 54 / 55, this is the one left, and it follows automatically.
trophies.name: Vice Got a Price!

steps.text: Earn every other trophy in this guide. The platinum is the reward for the full set, not a task of its own.
The last trophy most players earn is A Long Road (100% completion), so plan the grind around that, not around this one.

trophies.guide: A story trophy for Gone Fishing, the first main mission of Chapter 1. It unlocks by playing on and cannot be missed. A short prologue plays before Chapter 1 begins, so this is not the very first thing on screen.
trophies.name: Just Like Paradise

steps.text: Play through the prologue, then start Chapter 1 and finish the Gone Fishing mission.
Unmissable: every story mission trophy in this guide pops simply for finishing its mission.

trophies.guide: Finish every main mission in Chapter 1. The trophy pops at the chapter's end, when the story moves on. Start the save habit here: keep one manual save from the start of each chapter and one from its end, because missions cannot be replayed.
trophies.name: Paradise Lost

steps.text: Complete all Chapter 1 main missions in order; the trophy pops as the chapter closes.
Save manually at the chapter start and end. The game gives 15 manual slots and one autosave, and there is no mission replay.

trophies.guide: Finish every main mission in Chapter 2. The trophy pops as the chapter closes. Chapter 2 is where the two-character play opens up after Coffee Break, so several side chains and activities unlock around here — do the Chapter 1 balcony meditation (see Positive Mental Attitude) before you leave Chapter 1 behind.
trophies.name: T**s Ass Drug Money

steps.text: Complete all Chapter 2 main missions in order; the trophy pops as the chapter closes.
Before the chapter ends, check the Missables tab: the one possibly-missable trophy in the game lives in Chapter 1.

trophies.guide: Finish every main mission in Chapter 3. The trophy pops as the chapter closes. By now the contact chains are opening: Andy (Lucia only), Randy, Tyrone (Jason only) and Kenton all have strands that run across the later chapters, so keep talking to your contacts between missions.
trophies.name: Vice City, Baby!

steps.text: Complete all Chapter 3 main missions in order; the trophy pops as the chapter closes.
Between missions, answer contact calls: the side chains that end in trophies start in this chapter.

trophies.guide: Finish every main mission in Chapter 4. The trophy pops as the chapter closes and the story moves into its final chapter. Before you start Chapter 5, clear the at-risk list on the Missables tab — the finale is the point of no return for several strands.
trophies.name: Top Of The World, Ma

steps.text: Complete all Chapter 4 main missions in order; the trophy pops as the chapter closes.
Before Chapter 5, finish any open contact finales and the timed stranger strand. There is no mission replay after the story.

trophies.guide: Complete the final mission of Chapter 5. This is the story's end and the gold that closes the campaign. Free roam continues after the credits, so the open-world grind can wait — but anything tied to a story window cannot, so clear the Missables tab first.
trophies.name: You Gotta Know When to Get Off
trophies.risk: Point of no return: finish every at-risk item before starting the final mission.

steps.text: Before the final mission, finish the at-risk contact finales and the Chapter 1 meditation. Then play the finale.
After the credits, free roam stays open and the 100% checklist unlocks under Progress > Stats > 100% Completion.

trophies.guide: Complete the Breakfast Run story mission in Chapter 2. Like every mission trophy, it pops for finishing the mission and cannot be missed — just play the story in order.
trophies.name: Trust

steps.text: Reach Breakfast Run in Chapter 2 and finish it; the trophy pops at the mission's end.

trophies.guide: Complete The Cartel Heist story mission in Chapter 3. A heist mission, so expect a setup chain first: the trophy is for the heist itself, and it pops when the mission ends.
trophies.name: Break the Bank

steps.text: Play through the Chapter 3 setup missions, then finish The Cartel Heist itself.

trophies.guide: Complete the Child's Play story mission in Chapter 4. It pops for finishing the mission and cannot be missed.
trophies.name: Family Matters

steps.text: Reach Child's Play in Chapter 4 and finish it; the trophy pops at the mission's end.

trophies.guide: Complete the Headliners story mission in Chapter 4. It pops for finishing the mission and cannot be missed.
trophies.name: DWNFALL

steps.text: Reach Headliners in Chapter 4 and finish it; the trophy pops at the mission's end.

trophies.guide: Complete the VCIA Takedown story mission in Chapter 4. It pops for finishing the mission and cannot be missed. The airport itself matters later too: the hidden one-off Catch Me If You Can happens at VCIA.
trophies.name: Hi-Jacked

steps.text: Reach VCIA Takedown in Chapter 4 and finish it; the trophy pops at the mission's end.
Remember the airport layout: you will come back here for a secret trophy after the story.

trophies.guide: Complete the Operation Savage Glory story mission in Chapter 5. It pops for finishing the mission and cannot be missed — one of the last story trophies before the finale.
trophies.name: Snow Storm

steps.text: Reach Operation Savage Glory in Chapter 5 and finish it; the trophy pops at the mission's end.

trophies.guide: Attain 100% completion using the in-game checklist under Progress > Stats > 100% Completion. The checklist only unlocks after the story, but everything you do during the story already counts toward it, and nothing on it is missable. PowerPyx names this the hardest trophy in the game — not because any one item is hard, but because the list is long. It is also more forgiving than it sounds: the checklist is closer to 60% true completion, and only Robberies, Underwater Discoveries, Shooting Ranges, Drone Races and Bret's Quests need everything. You need 70 of 80 challenges, 100 optional missions (200–300+ exist, so missable ones do not matter), and each meditation spot counts +2 if you do it with both Jason and Lucia. See the Ledger tab for the full list.
trophies.name: A Long Road
trophies.risk: The longest grind in the game; start its pieces during the story.

steps.text: During the story, scan vehicles and study animals as you go, and do the optional missions: they feed the checklist.
After the credits, open Progress > Stats > 100% Completion and work the list in the Ledger tab's order.
Budget the bulk of the ~200-hour platinum here: the roadmap's Step 2 is about 100 hours on its own.

trophies.guide: Complete 250 stunts — jumps, airtime and stunt spots scattered across Leonida. There are 397 stunts in total, in four kinds: 130 stunt jumps, 202 under-the-bridges, 40 knife flights and 25 base jumps, and the 100% checklist wants 300 of them, so this trophy and the checklist overlap heavily. Under the Bridges runs are the quickest to clear. Track the count in Progress (Progress > Activities > Stunts, by region), and pick the easiest kind first; the counter is cumulative and stunts done during the story already count.
trophies.name: Cunning Stunts

steps.text: Do stunt jumps whenever you pass one; the count is cumulative and story stunts count too.
Use the count tracker on this trophy's card and clean up the remainder after the story with a stunt-spot guide.

trophies.description: Try each type of activity once.
trophies.guide: Try every type of activity at least once: the tracker counts 9 types (Progress > Activities), including the shooting range, races, fishing, arcade games, bowling and the rest. One taste of each is enough — you do not need to win or finish anything for this one. It is a sampler, so pair it with the other activity trophies: the first range visit, the first race and the first fishing trip all count here too.
trophies.name: Master of None

steps.text: Visit each activity type once: range, race, fishing, arcade, bowling and anything else the map offers.
Do it early: the first try of each activity feeds the deeper trophies (The Shootist, Top Fun, Baited My Tackle) later.

trophies.description: Earn a gold medal in all Shooting Range challenges.
trophies.guide: Earn a gold medal in every Shooting Range challenge — 42 golds in total, and all 42 are also required for 100% completion. The range is the Griffin Shooting Range at Rodgers Ranch. Golds are per-challenge, so you can chip away at them between missions; use the weapon each challenge is built for and replay a challenge until the gold time or score lands.
trophies.name: The Shootist

steps.text: Go to the Griffin Shooting Range at Rodgers Ranch and work the challenges one by one.
All 42 golds count toward the 100% checklist as well, so this is double duty, not a detour.

trophies.description: Win a Top Fun Drone Race at every location.
trophies.guide: Win a Top Fun drone race at every location. Guides report 14 race locations; the 100% checklist separately wants all 42 drone time trials, so winning the races and beating the time trials are two passes over the same activity. Learn each course's line first at a relaxed pace, then go for the win.
trophies.name: Top Fun

steps.text: Visit every Top Fun drone race location and win each race once.
Note the separate 100% line: all 42 drone time trials. Wins and time trials can be done in either order.

trophies.guide: Win 20 different races. Different is the key word: the same race won twice counts once, so work through the race list instead of farming your favourite. Street, off-road and water races all count as long as each event is a new one.
trophies.name: Earn Cash, Not Kudos

steps.text: Win 20 different race events; repeats of the same event do not add to the count.
Mix race types as you travel: a new event near your current mission is a free win toward the total.

trophies.description: Beat Cal in a fishing challenge.
trophies.guide: Beat Cal in a fishing challenge. Fishing unlocks after Feng Shui in Chapter 1, so this is one of the earliest activity trophies you can chase. A fishing challenge is a head-to-head: land the better catch under the challenge rules. If you lose, the challenge can be retried — it is not missable.
trophies.name: Baited My Tackle

steps.text: After Feng Shui in Chapter 1, find Cal and take the fishing challenge.
Out-fish him to win. A loss can be retried, so keep at it.

trophies.guide: Complete one arcade game — at the home console or an arcade cabinet. Any game, any cabinet: one full completion is enough. It also counts toward Master of None as your arcade activity.
trophies.name: Stick Fiddler

steps.text: Find an arcade cabinet or use the home console and complete one arcade game.

trophies.description: Complete the final mission for Andy.
trophies.guide: Complete the final mission of Andy's contact chain. Andy's strand is Lucia-only and opens from Chapter 3, so play it as Lucia and keep answering her calls between story missions. The finale only appears once the earlier Andy missions are done, so do not leave the chain half-finished when the story ends — the finale must be completed before the final mission.
trophies.name: Road to Rehabilitation
trophies.risk: At risk: Lucia-only chain; finish before the finale.

steps.text: From Chapter 3, play Andy's missions as Lucia whenever they appear.
Finish the chain's final mission before the story finale. Contact finales do not wait for cleanup.

trophies.description: Complete the final mission for Kenton.
trophies.guide: Complete the final mission of Kenton's contact chain, which runs through Key Lento after the Island Dreams mission. As with every contact finale, the chain must be finished before the story finale — do the Kenton missions as they appear rather than saving them all for after the credits.
trophies.name: This Was No Boat Accident
trophies.risk: At risk: finish the chain before the finale.

steps.text: After Island Dreams, follow Kenton's chain through Key Lento to its final mission.

trophies.description: Complete the final mission for Billy.
trophies.guide: Complete the final mission of Billy's contact chain in Kelly County, which opens after Coffee Break in Chapter 2. Billy's missions are out in the county, so fold them into your travel there rather than making a special trip at the end.
trophies.name: The Lone Rider
trophies.risk: At risk: finish the chain before the finale.

steps.text: After Coffee Break, follow Billy's chain in Kelly County through to its final mission.

trophies.description: Complete 8 mission strands for strangers across the state of Leonida.
trophies.guide: Complete 8 mission strands for strangers across Leonida — the Strangers & Freaks chains, marked on the map. One strand is timed, so do not ignore a stranger mission with an hourglass marker: timed quests expire, and while the guides say expired quests do not count against trophies, this silver needs 8 completed strands, so a lost one means finding another. Work the strands as they appear during the story.
trophies.name: Strangers & Freaks
trophies.risk: At risk: one strand is timed — do hourglass missions promptly.

steps.text: Take stranger missions as they appear on the map from Chapter 1 onward.
Prioritise any strand with an hourglass marker: timed quests expire.
Complete any 8 strands. The silver pops on the eighth.

trophies.description: Complete the final mission for Randy.
trophies.guide: Complete the final mission of Randy's contact chain, which opens after Clonin' Keys, Makin' Gs in Chapter 3. Play the chain as its missions appear; like the other contact finales, it must be wrapped up before the story finale.
trophies.name: Supply & Demand
trophies.risk: At risk: finish the chain before the finale.

steps.text: After Clonin' Keys, Makin' Gs in Chapter 3, follow Randy's chain to its final mission.

trophies.description: Complete the final mission for Tyrone.
trophies.guide: Complete the final mission of Tyrone's contact chain. Tyrone's strand is Jason-only and opens after Here, Kitty Kitty in Chapter 3, so play it as Jason. Finish the chain before the story finale.
trophies.name: Spin On This!
trophies.risk: At risk: Jason-only chain; finish before the finale.

steps.text: After Here, Kitty Kitty in Chapter 3, play Tyrone's missions as Jason.
Finish the chain's final mission before the story finale.

trophies.where: After Here, Kitty Kitty (Chapter 3) · Jason only

trophies.description: Meditate at every spot across Leonida.
trophies.guide: Meditate at every spot across Leonida — 18 meditation spots across 10 locations, some of them usable by both characters. This is the one potentially missable trophy in the game, and the miss lives in Chapter 1: after the mission Down to Earth, find Lucia at Jason's house in the morning. She says she is going to meditate and walks to the balcony — follow her, look at her, talk to her and choose Accept. That balcony meditation is not marked like a normal spot and it becomes permanently unavailable after Chapter 1. Whether the trophy actually requires it is still unconfirmed by the guides, so do it anyway: it costs a minute and protects the whole trophy. The last spots only open once you can play as both characters, after Coffee Break in Chapter 2.
trophies.name: Positive Mental Attitude
trophies.risk: POTENTIALLY MISSABLE — the Chapter 1 balcony meditation at Jason's house is gone after Chapter 1.

steps.text: Chapter 1, after Down to Earth: in the morning, talk to Lucia in the kitchen at Jason's house.
When she says she will meditate, follow her to the balcony and choose Accept when prompted.
After Coffee Break (Chapter 2), meditate at the remaining spots with both characters until the count hits 18.
It is still unconfirmed whether the balcony meditation is required — do it anyway. It is the only safety net.

trophies.description: Hunt a unique animal for Bret.
trophies.guide: Hunt a unique animal for Bret. Bret's chain is Jason-only and opens after Coffee Break, so play it as Jason and follow his hunting requests. Bret also has 15 Target Decks that feed the 100% checklist, so his strand is double duty.
trophies.name: Fair Game
trophies.risk: At risk: Jason-only chain; finish before the finale.

steps.text: After Coffee Break, take Bret's hunting missions as Jason.
Complete the unique-animal hunt he asks for. His 15 Target Decks are a separate 100% line — see the Ledger tab.

trophies.guide: Complete 3 collectible card sets. Cards are hidden across Leonida; a set is complete when every card in it is found. Guides report 18 sets in total, so you only need 3 — pick the sets whose cards cluster near places you already visit and leave the scattered ones alone.
trophies.name: Don't Touch My Deck

steps.text: Collect cards as you explore; a set completes when its last card is found.
Only 3 of the reported 18 sets are needed, so favour sets with cards near your route.

trophies.guide: WAiNK it at 100 locations — landmarks, curiosities, sculptures and tags across the map. WAiNK is the in-game photo/point-of-interest action: when a spot prompts you, do it. The counter is cumulative, so every landmark you pass while travelling is progress. Clean up the remainder after the story with a locations guide, working region by region so you do not re-cover the same ground.
trophies.name: You WAiNKer!

steps.text: WAiNK every landmark, curiosity, sculpture and tag prompt you pass while travelling.
After the story, sweep region by region with a locations guide until the counter reads 100.

trophies.guide: Complete 50 challenges. The game has 80 challenges in eight groups of ten, and the roadmap's Step 2 alone does 70 of them on the way to 100%, so this bronze will usually pop while you are working the checklist. Open Progress > Challenges to see the groups and pick the easy ones first — combat, driving and exploration groups fill up fastest in normal play.
trophies.name: One Last Thing

steps.text: Open Progress > Challenges: 80 challenges in eight groups of ten.
Complete any 50. The Step 2 grind toward 100% covers 70, so this pops along the way.

trophies.description: Lose a 4 star Wanted Level with your partner and escape the heat.
trophies.guide: Lose a 4-star wanted level with your partner and escape. It needs your partner beside you and the law fully shaken off — not just dropping to 3 stars. Build the heat together (a robbery is the natural way), then break line of sight, switch vehicles, and stay out of the search cones until the stars clear. It unlocks after Coffee Break, when the partner is available for open-world play.
trophies.name: Hot Together

steps.text: After Coffee Break, get your partner with you and raise a 4-star wanted level.
Break line of sight, change vehicles and stay hidden until all four stars clear.

trophies.where: After Coffee Break · with your partner

trophies.description: Rob 3 shops back-to-back with your partner without losing your Wanted Level.
trophies.guide: Rob 3 shops back-to-back with your partner without losing your wanted level. The trick is the opposite of Hot Together: here you must KEEP the heat. Plan a route with three shops close together, hit them in quick succession with your partner, and do not let the stars clear between robberies. A fast car and a short route matter more than firepower.
trophies.name: Retail Therapy

steps.text: With your partner, pick three shops close together on one route.
Rob all three back-to-back without letting the wanted level clear between them.

trophies.where: With your partner · three close shops

trophies.guide: Discover 100 vehicles. Scanning counts: point the scanner at a vehicle you have not logged yet (WAiNK app, hold up then R1) and it joins the collection in Progress > Vehicles. Scan as you travel — traffic, parked cars, boats and aircraft all have entries — and the total climbs without a dedicated grind. Story missions already put dozens of new vehicles in front of you. For the 100% checklist the bar is higher: 200 of the 277 base model vehicles.
trophies.name: Whip It Good

steps.text: Scan every new vehicle you see; the count lives in Progress > Vehicles.
Vary your routes: new districts mean new traffic, and new traffic means new discoveries.

trophies.description: Take down 5 enemies in a single use of Combat Focus.
trophies.guide: Take down 5 enemies in a single use of Combat Focus. One use, five takedowns — so you need a group, not a duel. Gang operations are the natural spot: they throw groups of enemies at you in one place. Trigger Combat Focus when five are in front of you and keep the chain going until the fifth drops. If the focus ends early, reset and try the next group.
trophies.name: Gunslinger

steps.text: Find a group of at least five enemies — a gang operation is ideal.
Trigger one use of Combat Focus and take down five enemies before it ends.

trophies.description: Make an unscheduled departure at VCIA.
trophies.guide: Make an unscheduled departure at VCIA — the airport. Guides point at gates E3 and E4 as the trigger area: get a plane moving and leave on your own schedule rather than the airport's. It is a hidden one-off, so expect the unexpected: the trophy's own description is the hint, and the airport is the place.
trophies.name: Catch Me If You Can

steps.text: Go to VCIA and head for the gates area (guides name E3 and E4).
Get airborne on an unscheduled departure — take a plane out yourself rather than following a scripted flight.

trophies.guide: A hidden one-off at the Mile Zero Air Station, built around the Rhino — the tank. The description is the hint: it involves the Rhino and heat. Head to the air station, find the Rhino, and do what the place invites you to do with it. As with the other secret trophies, the exact trigger is guide-reported rather than officially explained, so treat the location as the lead and experiment there.
trophies.mask: A secret at the air station
trophies.name: Challenging Tank

steps.text: Go to the Mile Zero Air Station and find the Rhino.
Use the Rhino there as the trophy's description suggests — the trigger is at the station, not in a mission.

trophies.description: Rob a jewelry store without being detected.
trophies.guide: Rob a jewelry store without being detected. Stealth is the whole trophy: no alarm, no witness, no chase. It unlocks after Yasmani's Jewelry Jobs in Chapter 3, which teaches the approach. Go in quiet, move when the staff look away, take the goods and leave before anyone notices. If the alarm trips, leave and retry — a detected run simply does not count.
trophies.name: Sneakthief

steps.text: After Yasmani's Jewelry Jobs (Chapter 3), pick a jewelry store.
Rob it without being detected: no alarm, no witness. If you are spotted, leave and try again.

trophies.guide: Rob 5 bank vaults and escape. Each vault is a full robbery: get in, crack the vault, get out with the law on you, and escape cleanly. It unlocks after That's Where The Money Is… in Chapter 4. Five escapes is a campaign, not a single night — do them one at a time between other work and let the heat die down between hits.
trophies.name: Maximum Withdrawal

steps.text: After That's Where The Money Is… (Chapter 4), rob bank vaults one at a time.
Escape cleanly after each vault. The trophy pops on the fifth escape.

trophies.where: After That's Where The Money Is… (Chapter 4)

trophies.description: Rob an Armored Truck and escape.
trophies.guide: Rob an armored truck and escape. Armored trucks run set routes in Chapter 4: stop one, breach it, take the cash and lose the wanted level that follows. A roadblock or a hard stop works better than a chase — pick a quiet stretch of road and hit the truck there.
trophies.name: A Classic Blitz Play

steps.text: In Chapter 4, find an armored truck on its route and stop it.
Take the cash, then lose the wanted level to complete the escape.

trophies.guide: Explore all of Leonida — clear the fog from the whole map. Every region visited, every road driven, until no grey remains. It is pure travel: drive, fly and sail into each corner, and the trophy pops when the last patch clears. Pair it with the collectible sweeps, since the same trips cover both.
trophies.name: The Goodtime State

steps.text: Travel into every region of Leonida until the map fog is fully cleared.
Combine it with card, WAiNK and vehicle sweeps: the same routes cover all three.

trophies.description: Rob an Illegal Operation belonging to each gang.
trophies.guide: Rob an Illegal Operation belonging to each gang — every gang, at least one operation each. Guides count 9 gangs and 39 operations in total, so you have a choice of targets per gang. Learn which operation belongs to which gang before you hit it, so a robbery counts toward a gang you still need rather than one you already have.
trophies.name: Pest Control

steps.text: Check which gangs you still need, then pick an Illegal Operation owned by one of them.
Rob one operation per gang until every gang is covered.

trophies.description: Enjoy a cocktail with a view on Ocean Beach.
trophies.guide: Enjoy a cocktail with a view on Ocean Beach — a hidden one-off at a rooftop bar. No mission, no chase: go to the rooftop bar on Ocean Beach, order the cocktail, and take in the view. It is one of the game's quiet secrets, and the trophy is the reward for finding the spot rather than for any skill.
trophies.name: In The Beginning…

steps.text: Go to the rooftop bar on Ocean Beach.
Order and enjoy a cocktail with the view. The trophy pops for the moment, not for a task.

trophies.description: Smash your way out of a vehicle showroom in classic style.
trophies.guide: Smash your way out of a vehicle showroom in classic style — the series' signature move: drive a car straight through the showroom glass. Guides name the South Vice City showroom and say the Key Cloner is needed to get the car moving first. Get the car, point it at the glass, and go. One clean exit is all it takes.
trophies.name: Capital Offense

steps.text: Go to the vehicle showroom in South Vice City with the Key Cloner.
Get a car moving inside, then smash out through the showroom glass.

trophies.where: South Vice City showroom · needs the Key Cloner

trophies.description: Follow-through at the Kolt & Associates' bowling alley.
trophies.guide: Follow through at the Kolt & Associates bowling alley — a hidden one-off tied to the Hit Kingpin Bowling optional activity in Chapter 2. Go bowling, and follow the shot through as the trophy's name suggests. It is a quiet optional moment, not a mission, so it is easy to walk past: make the trip in Chapter 2.
trophies.mask: A secret at the bowling alley
trophies.name: Let’s Go Bowling

steps.text: In Chapter 2, go to the Kolt & Associates bowling alley (Hit Kingpin Bowling).
Bowl and follow through on the shot as the trophy asks.

trophies.guide: A partnership with mass appeal — a hidden trophy about the duo, unlocked after Coffee Break when both characters are in play. The description is deliberately vague, but the shape is clear: it rewards playing the partnership, not a single character. Keep switching between Lucia and Jason and doing things together after Coffee Break, and it will come.
trophies.name: Personal Best

steps.text: After Coffee Break, play as both characters and do activities together.
The trigger is the partnership itself — keep both characters active rather than maining one.

trophies.guide: Choices made, for better or worse — a hidden trophy that builds through play. It tracks the decisions you make across the story rather than any single mission. There is no single trigger to chase: play the story, make the choices when they come, and it pops when the count is met. Note the warning on the Missables tab: some profiles and choices cannot be undone, so save before the big decisions.
trophies.name: Actions Speak Louder
trophies.risk: At risk: some choices cannot be undone — save before big decisions.

steps.text: Play the story and make the choices when they come; the trophy builds across them.
Save manually before major decisions: some profiles cannot be undone.

trophies.guide: Second time's the charm — a hidden one-off whose method the guides have not confirmed yet. As of 21 Nov 2026, no guide we read gives a verified trigger for this trophy, and this guide will not invent one. What we know: it is hidden, bronze, and its description hints at succeeding on a second attempt at something. Check back on the Sources tab's guides, or try the things in the game that ask for a retry — and if you find the trigger, it belongs in a guide update, not a guess.
trophies.name: Bad Luck, I Guess
trophies.risk: Unconfirmed: no guide has a verified method yet (21 Nov 2026).

steps.text: No verified method exists yet: KeenGamer notes some hidden trophy solutions are still being confirmed.
Do not trust a guessed method. The description hints at a second attempt — retry-based activities are the honest lead.

trophies.guide: What the hell just happened? — a hidden one-off in Kelly County, guide-reported after 2 AM. The guides have not confirmed the full trigger yet: the location and the hour are the lead, the rest is still being worked out. Go to Kelly County after 2 AM and look for whatever the night is hiding. If a method is confirmed after this guide's publication date, the Sources tab names where to check.
trophies.mask: A secret in Kelly County · after 2 AM
trophies.name: The Truth Is Out There
trophies.risk: Unconfirmed: location and hour are guide-reported; the full trigger is not verified yet.

steps.text: Go to Kelly County after 2 AM, as the guides report.
The full trigger is still unconfirmed — treat the hour and place as the lead, not a promise.

trophies.description: Bowl 'em over with a melee drive-by.
trophies.guide: Bowl 'em over with a melee drive-by — knock targets down with a melee attack from a moving motorbike. Guides report a 60-second window for the feat. Pick a stretch with pedestrians or targets, get the bike moving, and swing as you pass. It is a trick shot, so expect a few attempts before the timing clicks.
trophies.name: Ten Pin

steps.text: Get on any motorbike and build speed on a straight stretch.
Land melee drive-by knockdowns from the moving bike, within the reported window.

trophies.description: Earn $250,000 laundering Marked Bills through your contacts.
trophies.guide: Earn $250,000 laundering Marked Bills through your contacts. Marked Bills come from robberies and heists, and your contacts wash them for a cut. It unlocks after Credit Check in Chapter 3. The habit is simple: every time you hold Marked Bills, run them through a contact instead of sitting on them, and the $250,000 total arrives as a side effect of the crime grind.
trophies.name: Dime on the Dollar

steps.text: After Credit Check (Chapter 3), launder every Marked Bill you hold through your contacts.
Keep at it across the crime grind until the laundered total reaches $250,000.

trophies.guide: Spend $100,000 across all shops. Everything counts: clothes, weapons, food, car mods, property extras — any shop, any purchase. The total is cumulative across the whole game, and the crime and story spending along the way already covers much of it. If you are short at the end, car mods and clothes are the fastest way to close the gap.
trophies.name: Treat Yo Self

steps.text: Spend normally across all shops; the total is cumulative.
If short near the end, close the gap with car mods and clothes.

trophies.guide: Purchase all garage properties. Garages unlock after Daily Driver in Chapter 2: buy each one as it becomes available rather than leaving them for the end, since a garage is also where your collection lives. The trophy pops when the last garage is bought.
trophies.name: Little Boxes

steps.text: After Daily Driver (Chapter 2), buy each garage property as it unlocks.
The trophy pops on the final purchase.

trophies.description: Register 10 vehicles to the Scooter Bros app.
trophies.guide: Register 10 vehicles to the Scooter Bros app. The app unlocks after Moses's mission in Chapter 2: register the vehicles you already own or find, one by one, until the count hits 10. Vehicles you discover for Whip It Good are the natural candidates — scan first, register second, and two trophies move at once.
trophies.name: On the Spot

steps.text: After Moses's mission (Chapter 2), open the Scooter Bros app.
Register 10 vehicles. Pair it with Whip It Good: scan first, then register.
